cases.about: R4 and R5 with null values: the last observation is null, so the latest EFFR is the valued one before it and its previous observation skips a null; the recent table has fewer than 30 rows with nulls, and the windows end on the latest EFFR (leaving the trailing null out of the EFFR line) with change points that all begin after S.

R6: the month comparison date is a Sunday (the Friday before is used), the year comparison date is exactly 7 days after its observation (used) and the five-year one 8 days after (outside-window); the 1y window starts in the middle of a target segment and the longer windows start before the first change point.

R7 with a single valued observation after a null one: 'previous' has the reason 'no-earlier' and the other comparisons 'before-data', and without change points every window has no X0, no segments and no target.

R3 inside R7 with D = 2024-03-31: the month comparison date is clamped to 2024-02-29, the five-year date 2019-03-31 is a Sunday (the Friday before is used), and the previous observation skips a null record.

No observations: no latest EFFR, no comparisons and empty tables, R8 queries before the first change point, on effective dates and on the day before them, and windows built from the change points alone, with the rate to range switch inside them and the last change point at E.
Neither observations nor change points: no latest EFFR, no target in effect and no window at all.

R10 and R11 across kinds: rate to rate, the rate to range transition, a range change with unequal bound changes and a range to rate change, with comparison rows whose targets are of the other kind; the long windows hold three segments of alternating kinds and the last change point is at E.

R11: the month comparison is not shown (outside-window, from a Saturday back to a Friday 8 days before) and the year comparison's period is before the first change point, so its target and target change are null; the 1y window starts on an observation, which it includes.

R13: the last change point is effective after the latest EFFR period, so E is that change point's date and the last segment ends on it with no closing point, while the latest EFFR row still has the target in effect before it.

R13: the 1y window contains no change point, so its target is the X0 point and the closing point at E; the month and year comparisons are outside the 7-day window and the previous change is 1 basis point.
R12 with 33 observations: the recent table keeps the last 30, newest first, and the oldest row shown takes its previous observation from outside the table, skipping a null.

Rows copied from the verified appendix B fixture CSVs (test data, never a publication): the EFFR for July 2000, November 2016, November 2021, November 2025 and 2026-09-01 to 2026-11-18, with all 73 target change points; the observations are a subset, so the windows omit the EFFR line.
